report.headline: G League usage star projects to a modest, league-average NBA role, with shooting projection unreliable

projection.text: The model projects a usage rate of 19.2% in the NBA, down from 25.0% in the G League (+1.10 sd above that league's average), with an 80% interval spanning 14.0% to 24.5% — a range covering roughly two-thirds of a standard deviation in either direction around the target league's mean of 20.1% (sd 5.2%).

risks.text: Projected NBA usage (19.2%) falls well short of both the naive same-standing baseline (25.8%) and even the simple folk rule of 18.8% is close, suggesting a real, model-supported role reduction typical of this league move.

Projected true shooting percentage (53.6%) sits below the target league's average of 55.7% and below the subject's own source-season mark of 57.4%, but this projection should not be trusted: the model's error (4.7%) is no better than a trivial league-mean guess.

The true shooting interval is very wide, from 47.9% to 59.4% at 80% confidence and 44.8% to 62.4% at 95%, spanning more than two standard deviations of the league's spread (sd 5.0%), underscoring that little can be said about efficiency here.
Two full seasons passed between the source season and the move, adding uncertainty about how representative the 2015-16 numbers remain by the time of the 2017-18 transition.

strengths.text: The subject produced at a high level in the source season: 20.886 points, 5.779 assists, and 4.192 rebounds per 75 possessions, with a 26.1% assist rate and a 33.9% share of shots from three.
Efficiency in the source season was solidly above the G League average, with a true shooting percentage of 57.4% (+0.32 sd).
The historical rate at which usage carries across this transition is meaningfully positive (a slope of 0.531), and the estimate is grounded in a moderate sample of 45 prior GL->NBA transitions.

The player already stood out relative to peers who made this same move, sitting at +1.10 sd on usage in their own league, above the average standing (+0.27 sd) of players selected for this transition.

uncertainty.text: The usage projection's 80% interval (14.0%-24.5%) spans about 10 percentage points, roughly double the league's standard deviation of 5.2%, so the model can say this player will likely take a below-to-average share of possessions but cannot pin down where in that range; the true shooting projection, meanwhile, is not trustworthy at all, since its out-of-fold error (4.7%) is no better than simply guessing the league mean.
